new_statements.quote: [p. 179] "...notar los tipos de vocales que sufren cambios en su variante en las posiciones pretónica, tónica y postónica; es decir, a inicio de palabra, la base léxica y a final de palabra." [p. 73] "En Didza Xidza las siguientes reglas fonológicas son aplicables en vocales átonas en contexto final de palabra [...] 1a. /a/ → <Ø> / C_# [...] Por ejemplo, /nisa/ → [nis] 'agua'." [p. 111] "...la elisión de la vocal postónica a final de raíz..." [Anexo 4, p. 215] "ESTRUCTURA SILÁBICA: *CV (PRETÓNICA) -ꞌCV (TÓNICA) CV (POSTÓNICA)"
new_statements.translation: [p. 179] "...note the vowel types that undergo changes in one's variety in pretonic, tonic and post-tonic position, that is, at the beginning of the word, in the lexical base, and at the end of the word." [p. 73] "In Didza Xidza the following phonological rules apply to unstressed vowels in word-final context [...] 1a. /a/ → <Ø> / C_# [...] e.g. /nisa/ → [nis] 'water'." [p. 111] "...deletion of the post-tonic vowel at the end of the root..." [Annex 4, p. 215] "SYLLABLE STRUCTURE: *CV (PRETONIC) -ˈCV (TONIC) CV (POSTTONIC)"

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the lexical root ('base léxica'): in the inherited *CV-ˈCV-CV word template a prefixal syllable is pretonic, the first syllable of the (historically disyllabic) root is tonic, and the root-final vowel is post-tonic. The post-tonic vowel is variably deleted or reduced to ɨ (/nisa/ → [nis] ~ [nisɨ] 'water'), so many surface words are monosyllabic with stress on that single root syllable; enclitics such as =ru are unstressed. Phonemic forms in the thesis mark stress accordingly, e.g. /u2-ˈse32ʤi2=ɾu2/ 'desatar', /ˈɡa2ti2=ɾu1/ 'morir', /ˈbe2.la1/ 'víbora', /ˈpa2ni/ 'rebozo'. No explicit 'el acento recae en...' sentence exists; the reading is inferred from the terminology, the template and the transcriptions.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (the IPA secondary-stress mark is only explained in the general phonetics chapter, p. 41).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Laryngealized (checked, rearticulated) vowels are restricted to the tonic syllable and weak creaky vowels to atonic syllables (p. 124); pretonic vowels are also reduced or lost in innovative communities and by male speakers (pp. 46, 158).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (prefix + root + enclitic); citation forms elicited from eight Rincón communities (Tanetze de Zaragoza, Juquila Vijanos, Otatitlán de Morelos, San Juan Yaeé, Santiago Camotlán, San Juan Yatzona, Santo Domingo Roayaga, Santa María Temaxcalapa). Tone (3 level, 6 contour) is contrastive and carried by the tonic vowel; the thesis is an orthography-oriented phonological description.
new_statements.identity_note: Martínez Pérez 2019 describes Didza Xidza = Rincón Zapotec [zar] (Smith Stark's 'Zapoteco del Rincón Norte' communities Tanetze de Zaragoza, Juquila Vijanos, Otatitlán de Morelos, San Juan Yaeé, Santiago Camotlán, San Juan Yatzona, Santo Domingo Roayaga, plus Santa María Temaxcalapa from his 'Rincón Sur' group); the author is a native speaker from Tanetze. Southern Rincón Zapotec (zsr, sout3034-type separate code) and Las Delicias Zapotec (zcd, split by ISO change request 2021-040) are excluded by Glottolog from rinc1236; Temaxcalapa data in the thesis may belong to the zsr group. Yateé (Didza Xhon, zty) is explicitly excluded by the author.

sources.note: No explicit accent rule. Stress is handled implicitly: 'pretónica / tónica / postónica' positions are equated with 'inicio de palabra / la base léxica / final de palabra' (p. 179); Anexo 4 gives the word template *CV (PRETÓNICA) -ˈCV (TÓNICA) CV (POSTÓNICA) (p. 215); phonological rules delete or reduce unstressed word-final vowels, /nisa/ -> [nis] ~ [nisɨ] 'agua' (p. 73; 'elisión de la vocal postónica a final de raíz', p. 111); checked and rearticulated vowels occur 'en sílaba tónica', weak creaky vowels 'en sílaba átona' (p. 124); phonemic forms mark stress on the root after unstressed prefi…
